narrative: Fire emerges as a recurring pressure today, with protected tropical forests losing over four million hectares to stand-replacing fire since 2001 and Eastern Siberian boreal forests still showing shifted composition long after burning. Climate signals are more nuanced than simple range-tracking: a multispecies seed-addition experiment finds leading range edges lag warming while trailing edges do not, and microhabitat conditions, not just macroclimate, govern whether species actually establish in newly suitable areas. Animal movement and behaviour studies show indirect climate pathways matter as much as direct ones, from elephants curtailing movement during drought to a reef fish whose shoaling collapses because acidification simplifies its habitat rather than through warming itself. On the methods front, several new tools stand out: a transformer-based approach recovers energy-expenditure proxies from historical seabird biologging data, an open-source edge-device tool enables real-time animal re-identification in the field, and a validated Bayesian model converts nest temperatures into hatchling sex ratios for green sea turtles. Community and invasion ecology contributions include a superposition method that simplifies food-web trophic-position estimation, evidence that invasive freshwater bivalves lose parasite diversity in line with the enemy-release hypothesis, and a demonstration that invaders reorganise entire environmental axes rather than simply shifting niche overlap. Restoration and conservation findings range from two decades of Costa Rican forest-biomass recovery favouring active planting over natural regeneration, to Indonesian community-managed forests where connectivity, not management status alone, determines biodiversity outcomes. Evolutionary highlights include a model explaining how pathogens diversify their seasonal epidemic timing, and a global plumage-colour analysis across ten thousand bird species reconciling Gloger's and Bogert's rules as complementary rather than competing explanations.
